title: Block half-difference approximation
statement:
Let $n,m\ge0$, let $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $D(z)$ at every $z\in\mathbb R^n$, and suppose the map $D\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)$ is $C$-Lipschitz for some $C\ge0$. For a Boolean array $x=(x_{kl})_{k<n,\,l<m}$ and indices $i<n$, $j<m$, encode false by $1$ and true by $-1$, and write $S(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l<m}\sigma(x_{kl})$. If $x^{0}$ and $x^{1}$ are obtained by setting entry $(i,j)$ to false and true, respectively, then
\[\left|\frac{f(S(x^{0}))-f(S(x^{1}))}{2}-\frac{D(S(x))e_i}{\sqrt m}\right|\le\frac{2C}{m},\]
where $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector.
hypotheses_covered: $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ has derivative $D(z)$ at every $z$.
replaced: For $n,m\ge0$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times m}$, define $S_m(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=1}^m(-1)^{x_{kl}}$, interpreting division by zero as zero. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative family $D(z)$ that is globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$, with $C\ge0$. For any bit $(i,j)$, $\left|\frac{f(S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow0}))-f(S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow1}))}{2}-\frac{D(S_m(x))e_i}{\sqrt m}\right|\le2C/m$.
